subject: Applied Calculus

sourceBasis.syllabus: R-2025 Unit III: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, indefinite integrals, net change, improper integrals, arc length, area and surfaces of revolution.

note: Original ACADRIX 1-mark practice questions; not claimed official Anna University questions or verified PYQs.

questions.q: What is an indefinite integral?
questions.a: The family of all antiderivatives of a function, written with an arbitrary constant C.

questions.q: What is an antiderivative of f(x)?
questions.a: A function F(x) such that F′(x)=f(x).

questions.q: Why is an arbitrary constant C added to an indefinite integral?
questions.a: Because all functions differing by a constant have the same derivative.

questions.q: What is a definite integral?
questions.a: The integral of a function over a specified interval, representing an accumulated signed quantity.

questions.q: What does the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connect?
questions.a: Differentiation and integration.

questions.q: State the basic evaluation form of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
questions.a: If F′(x)=f(x), then ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx=F(b)−F(a).

questions.q: What is meant by net change?
questions.a: The accumulated change obtained by integrating a rate of change over an interval.

questions.q: If v(t) is velocity, what does ∫ₐᵇv(t)dt represent?
questions.a: The net change in position over [a,b].

questions.q: If r(t) is a rate of change of a quantity Q, how is the net change in Q found?
questions.a: By integrating r(t) over the required time interval.

questions.q: What is an improper integral?
questions.a: An integral with an infinite interval or an integrand that becomes unbounded within the interval.

questions.q: How is an improper integral with an infinite upper limit defined?
questions.a: As the limit of a definite integral as the upper endpoint approaches infinity.

questions.q: What is meant by convergence of an improper integral?
questions.a: Its defining limit exists and is finite.

questions.q: What is meant by divergence of an improper integral?
questions.a: Its defining limit does not exist finitely.

questions.q: What is arc length?
questions.a: The length of a curve between two specified points.

questions.q: State the arc-length formula for y=f(x) from x=a to x=b.
questions.a: L=∫ₐᵇ√(1+(dy/dx)²) dx.

questions.q: What geometric quantity can be found by integrating a suitable height function with respect to x?
questions.a: Area under a curve over the specified interval.

questions.q: What does a definite integral of a nonnegative function over [a,b] represent geometrically?
questions.a: The area under the curve and above the x-axis between a and b.

questions.q: What is signed area?
questions.a: Area counted positively above the x-axis and negatively below it in a definite integral.

questions.q: How is the total geometric area found when a curve crosses the x-axis?
questions.a: Split the interval at the x-intercepts and add the positive geometric areas.

questions.q: What is a surface of revolution?
questions.a: A surface generated by rotating a plane curve about an axis.

questions.q: What does the shell method conceptually use to generate a surface of revolution?
questions.a: Thin cylindrical shells formed by rotating strips about an axis.

questions.q: What does the disk/washer method conceptually use?
questions.a: Cross-sectional disks or washers perpendicular to the axis of rotation.

questions.q: State the power rule for integrating xⁿ when n≠−1.
questions.a: ∫xⁿdx=xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)+C.

questions.q: What is ∫1/x dx?
questions.a: ln|x|+C.

questions.q: What is ∫eˣ dx?
questions.a: eˣ+C.

questions.q: What is ∫cos x dx?
questions.a: sin x+C.

questions.q: What is ∫sin x dx?
questions.a: −cos x+C.

questions.q: What is the substitution method in integration used for?
questions.a: It changes the variable to simplify an integral, especially when a composite structure and its derivative occur together.

questions.q: What is integration by parts based on?
questions.a: The product rule for differentiation.

questions.q: State the integration-by-parts formula.
questions.a: ∫u dv=uv−∫v du.

questions.q: What does the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus imply about the derivative of an accumulated-area function?
questions.a: Under the usual continuity conditions, its derivative is the original integrand.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of an accumulation function?
questions.a: To represent the total accumulated effect of a rate or integrand from a reference point to a variable point.

questions.q: What is the geometric meaning of ∫ₐᵇf(x)dx when f changes sign?
questions.a: It gives net signed area, not necessarily total geometric area.

questions.q: What is the first step in many area-between-curves problems?
questions.a: Identify the bounding curves and determine their intersection points.

questions.q: What determines whether vertical or horizontal integration is more convenient for an area problem?
questions.a: Which choice gives simpler bounds and expressions for the region.

questions.q: What is the basic idea behind approximating a curve length?
questions.a: Replace the curve by many small line segments and take the limiting sum.

questions.q: What type of limit is involved in the definition of arc length?
questions.a: A limit of sums as the partition becomes finer.

questions.q: What happens to the interval length when the upper endpoint in ∫ₐ^∞f(x)dx is replaced by b?
questions.a: The improper integral is defined by taking the limit as b→∞.

questions.q: Can an improper integral converge to a finite value even though its interval is infinite?
questions.a: Yes, if its defining limit exists and is finite.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a convergence test for an improper integral?
questions.a: To determine whether the improper integral has a finite value.

questions.q: What is the net change in a quantity if its rate is r(t) from t=a to t=b?
questions.a: ∫ₐᵇr(t)dt.

questions.q: If acceleration is integrated with respect to time, what quantity change is obtained?
questions.a: The change in velocity.

questions.q: If velocity is integrated with respect to time, what quantity change is obtained?
questions.a: The change in position.

questions.q: What does C represent in an indefinite integral?
questions.a: An arbitrary constant of integration.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a definite and indefinite integral?
questions.a: An indefinite integral gives a family of antiderivatives, while a definite integral gives an accumulated value over bounds.

questions.q: What is the derivative of an antiderivative F(x) of f(x)?
questions.a: f(x).

questions.q: What does rotating a curve about an axis produce geometrically?
questions.a: A surface of revolution.

questions.q: Name one engineering application of integral calculus.
questions.a: Computing accumulated quantities such as displacement, area, volume or surface area.

questions.q: Why is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus important in applications?
questions.a: It allows accumulated quantities to be evaluated using antiderivatives and connects rates of change with totals.

questions.q: What is the usual condition on f for the basic Fundamental Theorem of Calculus evaluation?
questions.a: f should be continuous on the interval under the standard theorem statement.
